# Why C++ for Robotics {#sec-why-cpp}

## The Problem with Arduino

Most robotics beginners start with Arduino. That is not a criticism —
Arduino is an excellent tool for learning. The problem comes when you
try to go further.

When you call `digitalWrite(13, HIGH)`, Arduino writes roughly 50 lines
of C++ on your behalf. Those lines check pin validity, handle port
mapping, and manage timing. They are correct and safe. They are also
slow, opaque, and impossible to optimise.

## What You Actually Need

A robot needs three things from its software:

- **Determinism** — the control loop must execute in exactly the same
  time every cycle
- **Efficiency** — wasted cycles mean slower response and more heat
- **Transparency** — you must understand what every line does

Arduino gives you none of these reliably. Bare metal C++ gives you
all three.

## Mini Project — Bare Metal Hello World {#sec-ch01-project}

**Goal:** Blink an LED on a Teensy 4.1 using zero Arduino libraries.

**Hardware needed:**
- Teensy 4.1
- USB cable
- One LED + 330Ω resistor

**What you will build:**

```cpp
// Direct register write — no Arduino
#define LED_PIN 13
volatile uint32_t *gpio = (uint32_t *)0x42000000;

int main() {
    // Set pin as output
    *gpio |= (1 << LED_PIN);
    
    while(1) {
        *gpio ^= (1 << LED_PIN);  // Toggle
        for(volatile int i = 0; i < 100000; i++);
    }
}
```

**Expected output:** LED blinks at roughly 1Hz with no delay() anywhere
in the codebase.

**If it does not work:** Check that your toolchain is pointing at
arm-none-eabi-gcc, not the system GCC.
